result: Reviewed human UniProtKB entries, release 2026_03, read through rest.uniprot.org on 2026-10-21. SLC5A1 (P13866, SGLT1): Na+-coupled symporter of D-glucose or D-galactose with a Na+ to sugar ratio of 2:1, absorbing them across the apical brush-border membrane of enterocytes, with basolateral exit through GLUT2. SLC2A2 (P11168, GLUT2): facilitative transporter of glucose, fructose and galactose; likely mediates bidirectional glucose transfer across the hepatocyte membrane and glucose uptake by beta cells; expressed in liver, beta cells, small intestine and kidney. SLC2A1 (P11166, GLUT1): basal glucose uptake; present at the blood-brain barrier, where it carries glucose into the brain; detected in erythrocytes. SLC2A3 (P11169, GLUT3): highly expressed in brain. SLC2A4 (P14672, GLUT4): insulin-regulated; retained intracellularly in muscle and fat cells and translocated to the cell surface upon insulin stimulation. HK1 (P19367) and HK3 (P52790): allosteric enzymes inhibited by their product, glucose 6-phosphate. GCK (P35557): weak affinity for glucose, mainly expressed in pancreatic beta cells and liver, acts as the glucose sensor of the beta cell; at low glucose the inactive GCK-GCKR complex is recruited to the hepatocyte nucleus; variants cause maturity-onset diabetes of the young 2 and familial hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia 3. PFKL (P17858), PFKM (P08237) and PFKP (Q01813): catalyse the first committing step of glycolysis, need Mg2+, are allosterically activated by ADP, AMP or fructose 2,6-bisphosphate and inhibited by ATP or citrate. PFKFB1 (P16118): makes and degrades fructose 2,6-bisphosphate; phosphorylation at Ser-33 inhibits the kinase and activates the bisphosphatase; liver. GPI (P06744), ALDOA (P04075), ALDOB (P05062), ALDOC (P09972), TPI1 (P60174), GAPDH (P04406, with phosphate and NAD+), PGK1 (P00558, Mg2+), PGAM1 (P18669) and PGAM2 (P15259, with 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate as primer) and ENO1 (P06733), ENO2 (P09104) and ENO3 (P13929, Mg2+) catalyse reactions that run in both directions in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. PKLR (P30613): allosterically activated by fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, needs Mg2+ or Mn2+ and K+; variants cause congenital non-spherocytic haemolytic anaemia 2 with decreased red-cell pyruvate kinase activity. PKM (P14618): isoform M1 is active without fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, isoform M2 requires it. LDHA (P00338) and LDHB (P07195) interconvert pyruvate and lactate with NADH and NAD+. PDHA1 (P08559): with PDHB forms E1, which catalyses thiamine pyrophosphate-dependent decarboxylation of pyruvate and reductive acetylation of the lipoyl groups of E2; phosphorylation by PDK family kinases inactivates it and dephosphorylation reactivates it. PDK1 (Q15118), PDK2 (Q15119) and PDK3 (Q15120): inhibited by dichloroacetate. PDK4 (Q16654): up-regulated by prolonged fasting, down-regulated by insulin. CS (O75390): forms citrate from acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate. ACO2 (Q99798): isomerises citrate to isocitrate via cis-aconitate, with a [4Fe-4S] cluster. IDH3A (P50213): with IDH3B and IDH3G decarboxylates isocitrate to 2-oxoglutarate with NAD+; activated by citrate and ADP; high ATP inhibits. OGDH (Q02218): thiamine diphosphate-dependent, irreversible decarboxylation of 2-oxoglutarate; Ca2+ and ADP stimulate, ATP and NADH reduce its activity. SUCLG1 (P53597) with SUCLG2 (Q96I99) or SUCLA2 (Q9P2R7): couples succinyl-CoA hydrolysis to GTP or ATP synthesis, the only substrate-level phosphorylation of the cycle. SDHA (P31040): FAD-containing flavoprotein of complex II in the inner membrane, transfers electrons from succinate to ubiquinone. FH (P07954): reversible interconversion of fumarate and L-malate. MDH2 (P40926): reversible conversion of malate to oxaloacetate with NAD+.
